EVIDENCE.definition: Raw or directly inspectable artifact used to support or challenge a claim.

FACT.definition: A neutral, verifiable proposition grounded in evidence, with minimal interpretation.
FACT.example: Endpoint /users constructs a SQL query using string concatenation with user-controlled input.

FINDING.definition: An analytical conclusion derived from evidence and/or facts, such as a defect, vulnerability, regression, or inconsistency.
FINDING.example: Endpoint /users is potentially vulnerable to SQL injection.

OPINION.definition: A reasoned judgment or preference from a model or human that is not authoritative and may be unsupported by deterministic proof.

PROPOSAL.definition: A concrete recommended action or change offered for review. It is actionable but not authoritative until approved.

DECISION.definition: An authoritative approved outcome that governs implementation or policy until it is superseded or revoked.

classification_rules.statement: A security scanner report is EVIDENCE; the conclusion drawn from it is a FINDING.
If a statement can be checked directly against cited evidence with little judgment, classify it as FACT. If it interprets risk, impact, cause, or severity, classify it as FINDING.
Model-generated recommendations default to OPINION or PROPOSAL, never DECISION.
Only an authorized approval event may promote a proposal or draft decision into DECISION.

invariants: Facts and findings must remain distinguishable in storage and UI.
A finding may be urgent without becoming authoritative.
Approved decisions keep historical identity when later superseded or revoked.
